title: Greetings and goodbyes
subtitle: 인사
review: Written by Claude. The Korean and the romanization have not been checked by a Korean speaker. No audio yet: the Korean voice is not chosen. Burmese lines drafted by Claude. Check them before publishing.
intro: The phrases you need on day one. Read the romanization, and look at the Hangul under it as you go.

tr.my: မင်္ဂလာပါ။

lines.note: Morning, afternoon or evening. To friends: Annyeong.

tr.my: တွေ့ရတာ ဝမ်းသာပါတယ်။

lines.note: Only the first time you meet someone.

tr.en: Pleased to meet you. / I'm in your care.
tr.my: ခင်ခင်မင်မင် ဆက်ဆံပေးပါ။
ကျေးဇူးတင်ပါတယ်။

lines.note: A little softer and friendlier: Gomawoyo.
Literally 'no': the usual modest answer to thanks.

tr.my: တောင်းပန်ပါတယ်။
တဆိတ်လောက်။

lines.note: To call a waiter, or to stop someone in the street.
Said by the person who stays: 'go in peace'.

tr.en: Goodbye. (when you are the one leaving)

lines.note: Said by the person who leaves: 'stay in peace'.

tr.my: နောက်မှ တွေ့မယ်။

lines.note: Said to colleagues at the end of the day.

questions.q: You meet your new boss for the first time. What do you say?
questions.why: Mannaseo bangapseumnida is for a first meeting. Follow it with Jal butakdeurimnida.

questions.q: You are leaving a shop. The shopkeeper stays. What do you say?
questions.why: You leave and the other person stays: Annyeonghi gyeseyo, 'stay in peace'.

questions.q: A colleague is going home after work. What do you say?
questions.why: Sugohasyeosseumnida thanks a colleague for the day's work.
